I want you to solve GitHub issue #3757: implement the fix, validate it,
commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(`ls /workspace/*/bifrost` finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes,
fetch origin, and check out this exact commit detached: 0722dea6bcb52ef5335695a701631d157c31cbf4
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
No notification arrives between turns: never end your turn to wait for a
background command, because nothing will wake you. Poll it yourself in the
foreground, in waits of at most 5 minutes, and keep the turn running until the
FINAL REPORT is written.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.
If the build cache wrapper stalls (a cargo command that starts no compiler for
more than ten minutes), you may run that command through plain cargo
(/usr/local/cargo/bin/cargo) and say so in your report; do not move target/
or change shared cache settings.

Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer
cache at /workspace/cache when needed. Validate the actual witnesses and census
coverage, not merely a lower finding count caused by sampling or suppression.

dels for Rust std and framework inputs: `std::env::args`/`var`, stdin, HTTP headers, and Axum/Actix handler extractors (`Query<T>`, `Path<T>`, `Json<T>`), including handler parameters as entry points.
2. **SQL API contracts.** Reviewed models for SQLx, Diesel, rusqlite, postgres, and tokio-postgres. Separate the SQL text operand from bound values, and support generic, async, trait, and callback forms. A complete sink model must let analysis observe the SQL text at the call without the library body, and must leave unrelated effects open.
3. **Caller completeness at modeled boundaries.** A procedure whose only unknowns are modeled calls should get complete semantics. Confirm or refute the "likely" root cause above.
4. **Rust value construction.** `format!`, `+`/`push_str`, builders, closures, async fns, and trait-object dispatch.
5. **Shipped policy.** A general Rust request-to-SQL security policy that uses these models, so users do not have to write endpoint models for common libraries.

Keep the sound result contract: missing models stay visibly incomplete, with a diagnostic that names the missing model or capability. An empty result from incomplete discovery is never a clean result.

## Acceptance criteria

- A documented support matrix: the supported Rust sources, SQL sinks, sanitizers, and propagation shapes, and which remain incomplete.
- Positive fixtures: a proven source-to-SQL-text path with a complete run.
- Negative fixtures (parameterized, non-reaching, sanitized): proven no-flow with a complete run.
- The three-case sample above passes as a regression test, plus independent cases for each supported API family.
- The rerun CodeQL comparison on the sample gives matching complete results. Stretch goal: a real Rust web service with SQL.

## 1. Cause (confirmed, Rust form)

The issue's "likely" cause is confirmed: a modeled sink call did not close its caller's coverage. Evidence comes from the plan's own snapshot classification, which I printed with temporary debug code that has since been removed (`/workspace/evidence/probe-base.txt`, `probe-stmt-model.txt`). Several separate causes stacked:

1. **Receiver-adjustment gap tied to the call point, not the call.** With a call model on `Client::execute`, the gap that still opened the binding was `caller=api.rs.execute cap=Calls subject=Point "method receiver autoderef and autoref adjustments may invoke Deref..."`. A model of the call could not close a point-scoped gap.
2. **Implicit-Drop gaps with no possible discharge.** The base classification held `incomplete: CleanupControlFlow "a temporary discarded by a wildcard let may require immediate Drop"` in `api.rs.execute`, and `"values introduced by direct let bindings may require implicit Drop"` in the helpers. Their types (`Result<u64, ()>`, `Client`, `&self`) are stated only by declarations in other files.
3. **`&str` methods in the helpers were unresolved external calls** (`to_owned`, `len`).
4. **Findings used a stricter edge rule than the run.** Any unproven edge made a finding `possible`, even edges the run itself forgives.
5. **Zero-argument std sources were rejected by the selector compiler.** On the base, only 3 of 6 source endpoints compiled, with `CallBindingSelectorRejected` for `args`, `args_os` and `stdin`.

## 2. Changes and reasons

- **`e510764f2b`: callers of modeled calls now close.**
  - The receiver-adjustment gap is now call-site scoped with a `CallResolution` discharge. A proven method target never passes through a user `Deref`; the dispatch resolver keeps only a boundary there.
  - New `SemanticGapDischarge::DeclaredDropGlue` (IR v40). Its query-time proof is in `crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/rust/drop_glue.rs`.
  - A small reviewed `&str` method table in the Rust lowering.
  - Findings now use the run's own edge discharge (`open_edges_are_derived`).
  - Terminal call-binding rows are accepted for exact zero-argument calls.
  - The Rust lowering's adapter version moves to `rust-value-semantics-v15`.
- **`872c6b2cb2`: reviewed contracts, fixtures and 8 regression tests.**
  - Contracts in `tests/fixtures/rust-sql-taint/models`. Sinks select only the SQL-text operand by exact qualified identity. Call models are conservative may-propagate closures from the SQL text, bound values and receiver into the result and receiver, with no sanitize and no kill. They state in their review notes that other effects stay open.
  - The std model and source contracts cover `var`, `var_os`, `args`, `args_os` and `stdin`.
- **`2bb66fb7f1`**: open-core inventory for the new paths.
- **`4bf122f618`**: the drop-glue attribute check now reads attributes through the shared `outer_attributes` helper. The old sibling walk accepted `#[derive(Serialize)]`; a new public unit test caught this. Also pins the IR v40 digest.
- **`331dcf1759`**: an intermediate cause-ordering rule, superseded by `a25f6a6e86`. I left it in the history rather than rebasing, following the repo rule.
- **`a25f6a6e86`**: the plan now keeps every incomplete cause in input order. The diagnostic names the first cause that keeps the solved result from derived completeness. Before this, it could blame a modeled call ("no applicable model").
- **`7d51789331`**:
  - The Go IR-digest pin is refreshed for v40.
  - The `issue_2607` moved-`Vec` pin is updated. The drop is now decided by the declaration, and the unmodeled `Vec::new()` keeps that run open.
- **`b1f66d07e9`**: support matrix in `docs/src/content/docs/data-flow-and-typestate.md`, plus a CHANGELOG

## 6. Draft GitHub comment

I reproduced the three-case sample and confirmed the likely cause in its Rust form: a modeled sink call did not close its caller's coverage. Four gaps held the caller open:
- the method receiver-adjustment gap was tied to the call point rather than the call;
- implicit-Drop gaps on values whose type another file declares could not be discharged;
- common `&str` methods were unresolved;
- findings used a stricter proof rule than the run.

The fix ties the receiver adjustment to its call and adds a query-time proof that a declared type's drop runs no workspace code. It also lowers a small reviewed table of `&str` methods and lets findings share the run's rule. With reviewed postgres and rusqlite contracts that treat only the SQL text as a sink and leave other effects open, the sample now reports one definite, complete finding for case (a) and proves cases (b) and (c) clean. The issue's original policy has no call contract, so it still stays inconclusive, and it now names the missing contract. Source contracts select `std::env::var`, `var_os`, `args`, `args_os` and `std::io::stdin` exactly; those runs report `proven_by_summary` because an authored model closes the calls. Incomplete runs now name the first input the solved result leaves open, so they no longer blame a call that its model closed. The data-flow guide has a support matrix that names the missing model or capability for each incomplete row, including framework extractors, SQLx, Diesel, async drivers, macros, closures and the shipped policy. The reviewed models are test fixtures, so a shipped policy pack in bifrost-packs is the main follow-up.
